claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons have a high density of defects, internal stresses, and nanoscale phase fluctuations.
Nanoscale chemical and structural inhomogeneities are the primary governor of the low-field magnetocaloric response in this FeMnNiGeSi system.
Nanoscale chemical and structural inhomogeneities broaden the magnetic transition.
Mild post-deposition annealing reduces nanoscale chemical fluctuations and makes magnetic exchange coupling more homogeneous.
Mild post-deposition annealing reduces defect density in FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons.
Annealing at 0.5–0.7 Tm can promote partial atomic ordering without coarsening the nanoscale microstructure.
Mild annealing relieves internal stresses in the deposited FeMnNiGeSi material.
Reducing the distribution of local exchange interactions reduces the distribution of local Curie temperatures.
A narrower distribution of local Curie temperatures sharpens the magnetic transition.
Improved exchange homogeneity facilitates more coherent magnetic-domain switching.
Improved nanoscale magnetic homogeneity makes heat transfer more efficient during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealing will increase the peak magnetocaloric entropy change relative to the as-deposited state.
Annealing will produce a narrower and sharper magnetic transition relative to the as-deposited state.
Annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis and hysteretic energy losses during low-field cooling cycles.
Nanoscale disorder in the as-deposited material reduces its magnetocaloric effect.
Nanoscale disorder in the as-deposited material increases hysteresis through a broad distribution of exchange interactions.
Bulk and nanoscale forms can exhibit different magnetic transition behavior.
The proposed behavior applies near the intrinsic magnetic transition under low applied fields and may differ under high fields or in bulk samples.
